# Notes of this project for coding agents

Dennis Otto: The projects of Dennis Otto in one place: Home Assistant, Nextcloud and Paperless, GitHub automation and the blueprint they all share.

This file belongs to the project: the blueprint wrote it once, and its updates leave it alone. It adds to `AGENTS.md` what a coding agent needs to know about this project alone, such as its architecture, the commands of its own checks and what to watch for in its tests.

## Where things are

- `README.md` documents installation, configuration and use, `docs/` holds the pages of the website, and `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes of every release.
- `projects.toml` lists every project once; `.github/mkdocs_project.py`, the hooks of the website, turns it into the cards of both home pages, the table of `README.md`, the files at the root of the address, and on the Trust pages the guarantees that every project shares, the table of the numbers of each project, which a phone shows as a card for each with `docs/stylesheets/extra.css`, and the tabs of verify commands in place of `<!-- trust-shared -->`, `<!-- trust -->` and `<!-- verify -->`, from the `[trust]` texts and the optional `asset` key of each project. Its tests are in `tests/test_mkdocs_project.py`, with every line and branch covered.
- The line *Works with …* of a card comes from `requires` of its project in `projects.toml`: a text in every language, or a file of its repository, such as `hacs.json`, with the field of each value and a text with `{}`. The hooks read the file at the tag of the latest release of the build from `raw.githubusercontent.com` and take only a version from it, matched by `VERSION`; a file that can't be read leaves the line off without a warning, and the catalog bot reads the same file on the default branch. The tests read the files of the real projects from `tests/fixtures/requirements/`, never from the network: a new source in `projects.toml` needs its fixture there.
- The Releases page, `docs/releases.md` and `docs/releases.de.md`, gets the notes of the latest releases of every project in place of `<!-- release-notes -->`, and *What's new* of the home pages the latest release of each in place of `<!-- releases -->`: the hooks read them from the API of GitHub at the build and keep only text, lists, headings, tables, code and links to https of the notes, which take the place of their placeholders in `on_page_content`, after Markdown. Never let the HTML of a release reach a page another way; [decision 0005](../docs/decisions/0005-the-releases-page-takes-the-notes-from-the-api-at-the-build.md) says why.
- `scripts/check-site.sh`, which the check *docs* runs after the strict build with the folder `site`, runs `python3 -I .github/mkdocs_project.py --site site`: it checks in the built website what the hooks promise in the files that they alone write or change after the build, as the table in *The check of the built website* of `README.md` lists, and names each broken promise with its file and its fix. A hook that writes something new after the build gets its rule there too, with a test that breaks the folder of `hub_site` in `tests/test_mkdocs_project.py`; `bash scripts/check.sh` builds the website without it, so run it yourself after `mkdocs build --strict`.
- A project whose repository was renamed names the old folders of its website in `former` of `projects.toml`, and the pages of each old website in `former/<folder>.txt`. The hooks write a page at every old address that leads to the same page in the new folder, the 404 page of `overrides/404.html` leads every other address of an old folder there, and the card keeps the old anchor; [decision 0004](../docs/decisions/0004-the-root-website-keeps-the-old-addresses-of-a-renamed-project.md) says why.
- `docs/javascripts/projects.js` writes the live facts of the dashboard into the cards of the home pages and the `td[data-fact]` cells of the Trust pages as they load, a release newer than the build into *What's new* and the Releases pages, and the day of every release as the time since; `overrides/facts.html` loads it on those pages. Its tests, `tests/projects.test.mjs`, run with Node 20 or newer and no packages, `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`, on a document of their own; `scripts/check-project.sh` runs them with the tests of the hooks.
